celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿طسم﴾ Allah knows best what He means by it.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ i.e. these verses ﴿آيَاتُ الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Quran; the iḍāfa (genitive construct) is in the sense of مِنْ ﴿الْمُبِينِ﴾ which makes the truth distinct from falsehood.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿لَعَلَّكَ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿بَاخِعٌ نَفْسَكَ﴾ killing it with grief because ﴿أَلَّا يَكُونُوا﴾ i.e. the people of Mecca ﴿مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ And لَعَلَّ here is for expressing concern (ishfāq), i.e. have pity on it [your soul] by lightening this grief.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿إِنْ نَشَأْ نُنَزِّلْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ آيَةً فَظَلَّتْ﴾ in the sense of the imperfect, i.e. تَظَلُّ, i.e. would continue ﴿أَعْنَاقُهُمْ لَهَا خَاضِعِينَ﴾ and they would believe. And since the necks are described with humility, which belongs to their owners, the adjective derived from it is given the plural of rational beings.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَمَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ ذِكْرٍ﴾ Quran ﴿مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ مُحْدَثٍ﴾ an explanatory adjective (ṣifa kāshifa) ﴿إِلَّا كَانُوا عَنْهُ مُعْرِضِينَ﴾

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوا﴾ it ﴿فَسَيَأْتِيهِمْ أَنْبَاءُ﴾ the consequences of ﴿مَا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا﴾ look ﴿إِلَى الْأَرْضِ كَمْ أَنْبَتْنَا فِيهَا﴾ i.e. many ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ زَوْجٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾ fine kind.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَةً﴾ an indication of the perfection of His power, the Exalted ﴿وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ in the knowledge of Allah; and كَانَ, said Sībawayh, is redundant (zāʾida).

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ﴾ possessor of might, who takes vengeance on the disbelievers ﴿الرَّحِيمُ﴾ who has mercy on the believers.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember, O Muhammad, to your people ﴿إِذْ نَادَى رَبُّكَ مُوسَى﴾ on the night he saw the fire and the tree ﴿أَنِ﴾ i.e. بِأَنْ ﴿ائْتِ الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ as a messenger.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ together with him; they wronged themselves by disbelieving in Allah, and [wronged] the Children of Israel by enslaving them ﴿أَلَا﴾ the hamza is for the disapproving question (istifhām inkārī) ﴿يَتَّقُونَ﴾ Allah, by obeying Him, and so affirm His oneness.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِي﴾ from their denying me ﴿وَلَا يَنْطَلِقُ لِسَانِي﴾ in delivering the message, because of the knot in it ﴿فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَى﴾ my brother ﴿هَارُونَ﴾

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَلَيَّ ذَنْبٌ﴾ for killing the Copt among them ﴿فَأَخَافُ أَنْ يَقْتُلُونِ﴾ for it.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ the Exalted ﴿كَلَّا﴾ i.e. they will not kill you ﴿فَاذْهَبَا﴾ you and your brother — in it there is taghlīb (giving precedence) of the one present over the one absent ﴿بِآيَاتِنَا إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ مُسْتَمِعُونَ﴾ to what you say and what is said to you; the two are treated as a group.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿فَأْتِيَا فِرْعَوْنَ فَقُولَا إِنَّا﴾ each of us ﴿رَسُولُ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ to you

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿أَنْ﴾ i.e. بِأَنْ ﴿أَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا﴾ to Syria ﴿بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ So they came to him and said to him what was mentioned.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ Pharaoh, to Mūsā ﴿أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا﴾ in our dwellings ﴿وَلِيدًا﴾ small, close to birth, after his weaning ﴿وَلَبِثْتَ فِينَا مِنْ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ﴾ thirty years; he wore of Pharaoh's clothes and rode of his mounts, and was called his son.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ الَّتِي فَعَلْتَ﴾ that is his killing the Copt ﴿وَأَنْتَ مِنَ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ who deny my favour to you in raising you and not enslaving you.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ Mūsā ﴿فَعَلْتُهَا إِذًا﴾ then ﴿وَأَنَا مِنَ الضَّالِّينَ﴾ unaware of the knowledge and the message that Allah gave me after it.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿فَفَرَرْتُ مِنْكُمْ لَمَّا خِفْتُكُمْ فَوَهَبَ لِي رَبِّي حُكْمًا﴾ knowledge ﴿وَجَعَلَنِي مِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَيَّ﴾ its original form is تَمُنُّ بِهَا ﴿أَنْ عَبَّدْتَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ an explanation (bayān) of تِلْكَ, i.e. you took them as slaves and did not enslave me; you have no favour in that, because of your wrongdoing in enslaving them. And some implied at the beginning of the speech a hamza of question (istifhām) for disapproval.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ﴾ to Mūsā ﴿وَمَا رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ whose messenger you said you are, i.e. what thing is He? And since creatures have no way to know His reality, the Exalted, but know Him only by His attributes, Mūsā, upon him be blessing and peace, answered him with some of them.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿قَالَ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا﴾ i.e. the Creator of that ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُوقِنِينَ﴾ that He, the Exalted, created it; so believe in Him alone.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ Pharaoh ﴿لِمَنْ حَوْلَهُ﴾ of the nobles of his people ﴿أَلَا تَسْتَمِعُونَ﴾ to his answer, which does not match the question?

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ Mūsā ﴿رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ آبَائِكُمُ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ And this, though it is included in what preceded, enraged Pharaoh, and therefore

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَكُمُ الَّذِي أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ لَمَجْنُونٌ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here; the preceding entry leads into this ayah.]

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ Mūsā ﴿رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ that He is so; so believe in Him alone.

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ Pharaoh, to Mūsā ﴿لَئِنِ اتَّخَذْتَ إِلَهًا غَيْرِي لَأَجْعَلَنَّكَ مِنَ الْمَسْجُونِينَ﴾ His imprisonment was harsh: he would confine a person alone in a place under the ground, where he could neither see nor hear anyone.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ Mūsā to him ﴿أَوَلَوْ﴾ i.e. would you do that even if ﴿جِئْتُكَ بِشَيْءٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ a clear proof of my message?

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ Pharaoh to him ﴿فَأْتِ بِهِ إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ﴾ in it.

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿فَأَلْقَى عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِيَ ثُعْبَانٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ a huge snake.

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُ﴾ took it out of his bosom ﴿فَإِذَا هِيَ بَيْضَاءُ﴾ radiant ﴿لِلنَّاظِرِينَ﴾ unlike the dark colour it had had.

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ Pharaoh ﴿لِلْمَلَإِ حَوْلَهُ إِنَّ هَذَا لَسَاحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ surpassing in the knowledge of sorcery

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿يُرِيدُ أَنْ يُخْرِجَكُمْ مِنْ أَرْضِكُمْ بِسِحْرِهِ فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿قَالُوا أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ﴾ postpone their matter ﴿وَابْعَثْ فِي الْمَدَائِنِ حَاشِرِينَ﴾ gatherers

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿يَأْتُوكَ بِكُلِّ سَحَّارٍ عَلِيمٍ﴾ who surpasses Mūsā in the knowledge of sorcery.

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿فَجُمِعَ السَّحَرَةُ لِمِيقَاتِ يَوْمٍ مَعْلُومٍ﴾ and that is the forenoon of the Day of Adornment.

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿وَقِيلَ لِلنَّاسِ هَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُجْتَمِعُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here; it is explained in the next entry.]

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿لَعَلَّنَا نَتَّبِعُ السَّحَرَةَ إِنْ كَانُوا هُمُ الْغَالِبِينَ﴾ The question (istifhām) is to urge them to gather, and the hope is on the supposition that they [the sorcerers] win, so that they might continue in their religion and not follow Mūsā.

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَاءَ السَّحَرَةُ قَالُوا لِفِرْعَوْنَ أَئِنَّ﴾ with both hamzas pronounced fully, and with the second softened (tashīl), and with an alif inserted between them in both ways ﴿لَنَا لَأَجْرًا إِنْ كُنَّا نَحْنُ الْغَالِبِينَ﴾

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿قَالَ نَعَمْ وَإِنَّكُمْ إِذًا﴾ i.e. then ﴿لَمِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ﴾

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿قَالَ لَهُمْ مُوسَى﴾ after they had said to him, «Either you throw, or we will be the ones who throw» ﴿أَلْقُوا مَا أَنْتُمْ مُلْقُونَ﴾ The command in it is for permission to let their throwing come first, as a means to make the truth manifest.

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿فَأَلْقَوْا حِبَالَهُمْ وَعِصِيَّهُمْ وَقَالُوا بِعِزَّةِ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّا لَنَحْنُ الْغَالِبُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿فَأَلْقَى مُوسَى عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِيَ تَلَقَّفُ﴾ with omission of one of the two tāʾs of the original: swallows [variant: تَلْقَفُ] ﴿مَا يَأْفِكُونَ﴾ what they distort by their deceptive trickery, making their ropes and staffs seem to be snakes moving.

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿فَأُلْقِيَ السَّحَرَةُ سَاجِدِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿قَالُوا آمَنَّا بِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿رَبِّ مُوسَى وَهَارُونَ﴾ because they knew that what they had witnessed of the staff could not come about by sorcery.

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ Pharaoh ﴿أَآمَنْتُمْ﴾ with both hamzas pronounced fully, and with the second changed into an alif [آمَنْتُمْ] ﴿لَهُ﴾ in Mūsā ﴿قَبْلَ أَنْ آذَنَ﴾ I ﴿لَكُمْ إِنَّهُ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ الَّذِي عَلَّمَكُمُ السِّحْرَ﴾ so he taught you part of it and overcame you with another ﴿فَلَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ what will befall you from me ﴿لَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ مِنْ خِلَافٍ﴾ i.e. the right hand of each one and his left foot ﴿وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿قَالُوا لَا ضَيْرَ﴾ no harm to us in that ﴿إِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا﴾ after our death, in whatever way it comes ﴿مُنْقَلِبُونَ﴾ returning, in the Hereafter.

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿إِنَّا نَطْمَعُ﴾ we hope ﴿أَنْ يَغْفِرَ لَنَا رَبُّنَا خَطَايَانَا أَنْ﴾ i.e. بِأَنْ (because) ﴿كُنَّا أَوَّلَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ in our time.

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿وَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى مُوسَى﴾ after years he stayed among them calling them with the signs of Allah to the truth, while they only increased in insolence ﴿أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِي﴾ the Children of Israel — and in one reading with kasra on the nūn and the connecting hamza (hamzat waṣl) in أَسْرِ, from سَرَى, a dialect form of أَسْرَى, i.e. travel with them by night to the sea ﴿إِنَّكُمْ مُتَّبَعُونَ﴾ Pharaoh and his troops will follow you and will plunge into the sea after you, and I will save you and drown them.

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿فَأَرْسَلَ فِرْعَوْنُ﴾ when he was told of their departure ﴿فِي الْمَدَائِنِ﴾ it is said that he had a thousand cities and twelve thousand villages ﴿حَاشِرِينَ﴾ gathering the army, saying:

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿إِنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ لَشِرْذِمَةٌ﴾ a band ﴿قَلِيلُونَ﴾ It is said that they were six hundred and seventy thousand, and the vanguard of his army was seven hundred thousand; he made them few in comparison with the great size of his army.

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿وَإِنَّهُمْ لَنَا لَغَائِظُونَ﴾ doing what enrages us.

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿وَإِنَّا لَجَمِيعٌ حَذِرُونَ﴾ alert; and in one reading [حَاذِرُونَ] prepared. Allah the Exalted said:

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿فَأَخْرَجْنَاهُمْ﴾ i.e. Pharaoh and his people, from Egypt, to overtake Mūsā and his people ﴿مِنْ جَنَّاتٍ﴾ orchards that were on both banks of the Nile ﴿وَعُيُونٍ﴾ streams flowing in the houses from the Nile

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿وَكُنُوزٍ﴾ visible wealth of gold and silver; it is called «treasures» because he did not give the right of Allah the Exalted from it ﴿وَمَقَامٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾ a fine assembly for the princes and ministers, surrounded by their followers.

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ was Our expelling, as We have described ﴿وَأَوْرَثْنَاهَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ after the drowning of Pharaoh and his people.

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿فَأَتْبَعُوهُمْ﴾ they overtook them ﴿مُشْرِقِينَ﴾ at the time of sunrise.

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا تَرَاءَى الْجَمْعَانِ﴾ i.e. each of them saw the other ﴿قَالَ أَصْحَابُ مُوسَى إِنَّا لَمُدْرَكُونَ﴾ Pharaoh's host will overtake us, and we have no power against it.

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ Mūsā ﴿كَلَّا﴾ i.e. they will never overtake us ﴿إِنَّ مَعِيَ رَبِّي﴾ with His help ﴿سَيَهْدِينِ﴾ the way of salvation. Allah the Exalted said:

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿فَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى مُوسَى أَنِ اضْرِبْ بِعَصَاكَ الْبَحْرَ﴾ so he struck it ﴿فَانْفَلَقَ﴾ and it split into twelve parts ﴿فَكَانَ كُلُّ فِرْقٍ كَالطَّوْدِ الْعَظِيمِ﴾ the massive mountain; between them were paths which they travelled, and neither the saddle of a rider nor its felt got wet.

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿وَأَزْلَفْنَا﴾ We brought near ﴿ثَمَّ﴾ there ﴿الْآخَرِينَ﴾ Pharaoh and his people, until they travelled their paths.

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿وَأَنْجَيْنَا مُوسَى وَمَنْ مَعَهُ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾ by bringing them out of the sea in the state mentioned.

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنَا الْآخَرِينَ﴾ Pharaoh and his people, by closing the sea over them when they had fully entered the sea and the Children of Israel had come out of it.

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. the drowning of Pharaoh and his people ﴿لَآيَةً﴾ a lesson for those after them ﴿وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ in Allah; none of them believed except Āsiya, Pharaoh's wife; Ḥizqīl, the believer of Pharaoh's family; and Maryam bint Nāmūsā, who showed [them] the bones of Yūsuf, upon him be peace.

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ﴾ so He took vengeance on the disbelievers by drowning them ﴿الرَّحِيمُ﴾ to the believers, so He saved them from drowning.

celaleyn:69-69.t: ﴿وَاتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca ﴿نَبَأَ﴾ the account of ﴿إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ and a badal (substitute) is made from it:

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here; the preceding entry states that this is a badal from نَبَأَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ.]

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿قَالُوا نَعْبُدُ أَصْنَامًا﴾ they stated the verb explicitly in order to conjoin to it ﴿فَنَظَلُّ لَهَا عَاكِفِينَ﴾ i.e. we spend the day in worshipping them; they added it to the answer out of pride in it.

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿أَوْ يَنْفَعُونَكُمْ﴾ if you worship them ﴿أَوْ يَضُرُّونَ﴾ you, if you do not worship them?

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿قَالُوا بَلْ وَجَدْنَا آبَاءَنَا كَذَلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ i.e. like what we do.

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿قَالَ أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ مَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْبُدُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:76-76.t: ﴿أَنْتُمْ وَآبَاؤُكُمُ الْأَقْدَمُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:77-77.t: ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِي﴾ I do not worship them ﴿إِلَّا﴾ but ﴿رَبَّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ Him I worship

celaleyn:78-78.t: ﴿الَّذِي خَلَقَنِي فَهُوَ يَهْدِينِ﴾ to the religion.

celaleyn:79-79.t: ﴿وَالَّذِي هُوَ يُطْعِمُنِي وَيَسْقِينِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:80-80.t: ﴿وَإِذَا مَرِضْتُ فَهُوَ يَشْفِينِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:81-81.t: ﴿وَالَّذِي يُمِيتُنِي ثُمَّ يُحْيِينِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:82-82.t: ﴿وَالَّذِي أَطْمَعُ﴾ I hope ﴿أَنْ يَغْفِرَ لِي خَطِيئَتِي يَوْمَ الدِّينِ﴾ i.e. of recompense.

celaleyn:83-83.t: ﴿رَبِّ هَبْ لِي حُكْمًا﴾ knowledge ﴿وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِالصَّالِحِينَ﴾ the prophets.

celaleyn:84-84.t: ﴿وَاجْعَلْ لِي لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ﴾ good praise ﴿فِي الْآخِرِينَ﴾ who come after me until the Day of Resurrection.

celaleyn:85-85.t: ﴿وَاجْعَلْنِي مِنْ وَرَثَةِ جَنَّةِ النَّعِيمِ﴾ of those who are given it.

celaleyn:86-86.t: ﴿وَاغْفِرْ لِأَبِي إِنَّهُ كَانَ مِنَ الضَّالِّينَ﴾ by turning to him in forgiveness and so forgiving him; and this was before it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, as mentioned in Sura Barāʾa.

celaleyn:87-87.t: ﴿وَلَا تُخْزِنِي﴾ disgrace me ﴿يَوْمَ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾ i.e. people.

celaleyn:88-88.t: ﴿يَوْمَ لَا يَنْفَعُ مَالٌ وَلَا بَنُونَ﴾ anyone

celaleyn:89-89.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾ but ﴿مَنْ أَتَى اللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ﴾ from polytheism and hypocrisy, and that is the heart of the believer; that will benefit him.

celaleyn:90-90.t: ﴿وَأُزْلِفَتِ الْجَنَّةُ﴾ brought near ﴿لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ so they see it.

celaleyn:92-92.t: ﴿وَقِيلَ لَهُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْبُدُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:93-93.t: ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him, of the idols ﴿هَلْ يَنْصُرُونَكُمْ﴾ by warding off the punishment from you ﴿أَوْ يَنْتَصِرُونَ﴾ by warding it off from themselves? No.

celaleyn:95-95.t: ﴿وَجُنُودُ إِبْلِيسَ﴾ his followers and those who obeyed him among jinn and humans ﴿أَجْمَعُونَ﴾

celaleyn:96-96.t: ﴿قَالُوا﴾ i.e. those who went astray ﴿وَهُمْ فِيهَا يَخْتَصِمُونَ﴾ with those they worshipped:

celaleyn:97-97.t: ﴿تَاللَّهِ إِنْ﴾ lightened from the heavy [إِنَّ], and its noun (ism) is omitted, i.e. إِنَّهُ ﴿كُنَّا لَفِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ clear

celaleyn:99-99.t: ﴿وَمَا أَضَلَّنَا﴾ from guidance ﴿إِلَّا الْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾ the devils, or our forebears whom we followed.

celaleyn:100-100.t: ﴿فَمَا لَنَا مِنْ شَافِعِينَ﴾ as the believers have, of the angels, the prophets and the believers

celaleyn:101-101.t: ﴿وَلَا صَدِيقٍ حَمِيمٍ﴾ i.e. who cares about our situation.

celaleyn:102-102.t: ﴿فَلَوْ أَنَّ لَنَا كَرَّةً﴾ a return to the world ﴿فَنَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ لَوْ here is for wishing (tamannī), and نَكُونَ is its answer.

celaleyn:103-103.t: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ﴾ which is mentioned of the story of Ibrāhīm and his people ﴿لَآيَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾

celaleyn:104-104.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:105-105.t: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾ by their denying him, since they [the messengers] share in bringing the message of Allah's oneness; or because, owing to his long stay among them, he is as though [many] messengers. And قَوْم is made feminine with regard to its meaning, and masculine with regard to its wording.

celaleyn:106-106.t: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ﴾ by lineage ﴿نُوحٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ﴾ Allah?

celaleyn:107-107.t: ﴿إِنِّي لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ﴾ in conveying what I have been sent with.

celaleyn:108-108.t: ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ﴾ in what I command you, of affirming the oneness of Allah and obeying Him.

celaleyn:109-109.t: ﴿وَمَا أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ﴾ for conveying it ﴿مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ﴾ not ﴿أَجْرِيَ﴾ i.e. my reward ﴿إِلَّا عَلَى رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:110-110.t: ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ﴾ He repeated it for emphasis.

celaleyn:111-111.t: ﴿قَالُوا أَنُؤْمِنُ﴾ believe ﴿لَكَ﴾ your word ﴿وَاتَّبَعَكَ﴾ and in one reading [وَأَتْبَاعُكَ], plural of تَابِع, a mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿الْأَرْذَلُونَ﴾ the lowly, such as weavers and cobblers?

celaleyn:112-112.t: ﴿قَالَ وَمَا عِلْمِي﴾ i.e. what knowledge do I have ﴿بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾

celaleyn:113-113.t: ﴿إِنْ﴾ not ﴿حِسَابُهُمْ إِلَّا عَلَى رَبِّي﴾ and He will recompense them ﴿لَوْ تَشْعُرُونَ﴾ if you knew that, you would not find fault with them.

celaleyn:114-114.t: ﴿وَمَا أَنَا بِطَارِدِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:115-115.t: ﴿إِنْ﴾ not ﴿أَنَا إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ clear in warning.

celaleyn:116-116.t: ﴿قَالُوا لَئِنْ لَمْ تَنْتَهِ يَا نُوحُ﴾ from what you say to us ﴿لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمَرْجُومِينَ﴾ with stones or with abuse.

celaleyn:118-118.t: ﴿فَافْتَحْ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُمْ فَتْحًا﴾ i.e. judge ﴿وَنَجِّنِي وَمَنْ مَعِيَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ Allah the Exalted said:

celaleyn:119-119.t: ﴿فَأَنْجَيْنَاهُ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ فِي الْفُلْكِ الْمَشْحُونِ﴾ filled with people, animals and birds.

celaleyn:120-120.t: ﴿ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنَا بَعْدُ﴾ i.e. after saving them ﴿الْبَاقِينَ﴾ of his people.

celaleyn:121-121.t: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:122-122.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:123-123.t: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ عَادٌ الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:124-124.t: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ هُودٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:125-125.t: ﴿إِنِّي لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:126-126.t: ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:127-127.t: ﴿وَمَا أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ﴾ not ﴿أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:128-128.t: ﴿أَتَبْنُونَ بِكُلِّ رِيعٍ﴾ elevated place ﴿آيَةً﴾ a building as a landmark for passers-by ﴿تَعْبَثُونَ﴾ with those who pass by you, mocking them; and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of تَبْنُونَ.

celaleyn:129-129.t: ﴿وَتَتَّخِذُونَ مَصَانِعَ﴾ for water under the ground ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ﴾ as though you ﴿تَخْلُدُونَ﴾ in them, not dying.

celaleyn:130-130.t: ﴿وَإِذَا بَطَشْتُمْ﴾ by striking or killing ﴿بَطَشْتُمْ جَبَّارِينَ﴾ without compassion.

celaleyn:131-131.t: ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ in that ﴿وَأَطِيعُونِ﴾ in what I have commanded you.

celaleyn:132-132.t: ﴿وَاتَّقُوا الَّذِي أَمَدَّكُمْ﴾ bestowed favours on you ﴿بِمَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:133-133.t: ﴿أَمَدَّكُمْ بِأَنْعَامٍ وَبَنِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:135-135.t: ﴿إِنِّي أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾ in this world and the Hereafter, if you disobey me.

celaleyn:136-136.t: ﴿قَالُوا سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْنَا﴾ equal to us ﴿أَوَعَظْتَ أَمْ لَمْ تَكُنْ مِنَ الْوَاعِظِينَ﴾ at all; i.e. we will not desist because of your admonition.

celaleyn:137-137.t: ﴿إِنْ﴾ not ﴿هَذَا﴾ with which you have threatened us ﴿إِلَّا خَلْقُ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ i.e. their fabrication and their lies; and in one reading with ḍamma on the khāʾ and the lām [خُلُقُ], i.e. this [belief] we hold, that there is no resurrection, is nothing but the custom of the ancients, i.e. their nature and habits.

celaleyn:138-138.t: ﴿وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُعَذَّبِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:139-139.t: ﴿فَكَذَّبُوهُ﴾ regarding the punishment ﴿فَأَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ﴾ in this world, by the wind ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾

celaleyn:140-140.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:141-141.t: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:142-142.t: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ صَالِحٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:143-143.t: ﴿إِنِّي لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:144-144.t: ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:145-145.t: ﴿وَمَا أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ﴾ not ﴿أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:146-146.t: ﴿أَتُتْرَكُونَ فِي مَا هَاهُنَا﴾ of good things ﴿آمِنِينَ﴾

celaleyn:147-147.t: ﴿فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:149-149.t: ﴿وَتَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ الْجِبَالِ بُيُوتًا فَرِهِينَ﴾ exultant; and in one reading [فَارِهِينَ] skilful.

celaleyn:150-150.t: ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ﴾ in what I have commanded you.

celaleyn:151-151.t: ﴿وَلَا تُطِيعُوا أَمْرَ الْمُسْرِفِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:152-152.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يُفْسِدُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ by acts of disobedience ﴿وَلَا يُصْلِحُونَ﴾ by obedience to Allah.

celaleyn:153-153.t: ﴿قَالُوا إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مِنَ الْمُسَحَّرِينَ﴾ those who have been bewitched many times until their minds were overpowered.

celaleyn:154-154.t: ﴿مَا أَنْتَ﴾ also ﴿إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُنَا فَأْتِ بِآيَةٍ إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ﴾ in your message.

celaleyn:155-155.t: ﴿قَالَ هَذِهِ نَاقَةٌ لَهَا شِرْبٌ﴾ a share of the water ﴿وَلَكُمْ شِرْبُ يَوْمٍ مَعْلُومٍ﴾

celaleyn:156-156.t: ﴿وَلَا تَمَسُّوهَا بِسُوءٍ فَيَأْخُذَكُمْ عَذَابُ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾ because of the greatness of the punishment.

celaleyn:157-157.t: ﴿فَعَقَرُوهَا﴾ i.e. some of them hamstrung her with their consent ﴿فَأَصْبَحُوا نَادِمِينَ﴾ for hamstringing her.

celaleyn:158-158.t: ﴿فَأَخَذَهُمُ الْعَذَابُ﴾ that had been promised, and they perished ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾

celaleyn:159-159.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:160-160.t: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ لُوطٍ الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:161-161.t: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ لُوطٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:162-162.t: ﴿إِنِّي لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:163-163.t: ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:164-164.t: ﴿وَمَا أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ﴾ not ﴿أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:165-165.t: ﴿أَتَأْتُونَ الذُّكْرَانَ مِنَ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ i.e. of mankind

celaleyn:166-166.t: ﴿وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ مِنْ أَزْوَاجِكُمْ﴾ i.e. their private parts ﴿بَلْ أَنْتُمْ قَوْمٌ عَادُونَ﴾ transgressing from the lawful to the forbidden.

celaleyn:167-167.t: ﴿قَالُوا لَئِنْ لَمْ تَنْتَهِ يَا لُوطُ﴾ from your censure of us ﴿لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُخْرَجِينَ﴾ from our town.

celaleyn:168-168.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ Lūṭ ﴿إِنِّي لِعَمَلِكُمْ مِنَ الْقَالِينَ﴾ those who detest

celaleyn:169-169.t: ﴿رَبِّ نَجِّنِي وَأَهْلِي مِمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ i.e. from its punishment.

celaleyn:170-170.t: ﴿فَنَجَّيْنَاهُ وَأَهْلَهُ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:171-171.t: ﴿إِلَّا عَجُوزًا﴾ his wife ﴿فِي الْغَابِرِينَ﴾ those who remained — We destroyed her.

celaleyn:173-173.t: ﴿وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ مَطَرًا﴾ stones, as part of the destruction ﴿فَسَاءَ مَطَرُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ﴾ their rain.

celaleyn:174-174.t: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:175-175.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:176-176.t: ﴿كَذَّبَ أَصْحَابُ الْأَيْكَةِ﴾ and in one reading with omission of the hamza, transferring its vowel to the lām, and with fatḥa on the hāʾ; it is a thicket of trees near Madyan ﴿الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾

celaleyn:177-177.t: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ شُعَيْبٌ﴾ He did not say «their brother», because he was not one of them ﴿أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ﴾

celaleyn:178-178.t: ﴿إِنِّي لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:179-179.t: ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:180-180.t: ﴿وَمَا أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ﴾ not ﴿أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:181-181.t: ﴿أَوْفُوا الْكَيْلَ﴾ give it in full ﴿وَلَا تَكُونُوا مِنَ الْمُخْسِرِينَ﴾ those who give short measure.

celaleyn:183-183.t: ﴿وَلَا تَبْخَسُوا النَّاسَ أَشْيَاءَهُمْ﴾ do not diminish anything of their right ﴿وَلَا تَعْثَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ﴾ by killing and other things — from عَثِيَ, with kasra on the three-dotted letter [thāʾ]: to cause corruption; and مُفْسِدِينَ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) that emphasises the meaning of its governing word (ʿāmil).

celaleyn:185-185.t: ﴿قَالُوا إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مِنَ الْمُسَحَّرِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:186-186.t: ﴿وَمَا أَنْتَ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُنَا وَإِنْ﴾ lightened from the heavy [إِنَّ], and its noun (ism) is omitted, i.e. إِنَّهُ ﴿نَظُنُّكَ لَمِنَ الْكَاذِبِينَ﴾

celaleyn:187-187.t: ﴿فَأَسْقِطْ عَلَيْنَا كِسْفًا﴾ with sukūn and fatḥa on the sīn [كِسَفًا]: a piece ﴿مِنَ السَّمَاءِ إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ﴾ in your message.

celaleyn:188-188.t: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّي أَعْلَمُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ and He will recompense you for it.

celaleyn:189-189.t: ﴿فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَخَذَهُمْ عَذَابُ يَوْمِ الظُّلَّةِ﴾ it is a cloud that shaded them after intense heat had struck them; then it rained fire upon them and they were burnt ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾

celaleyn:190-190.t: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:191-191.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:194-194.t: ﴿عَلَى قَلْبِكَ لِتَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُنْذِرِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:195-195.t: ﴿بِلِسَانٍ عَرَبِيٍّ مُبِينٍ﴾ clear. And in one reading with doubling in نَزَّلَ and the accusative of الرُّوح, the fāʿil (agent) being Allah.

celaleyn:196-196.t: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ﴾ i.e. the mention of the Quran sent down to Muhammad ﴿لَفِي زُبُرِ﴾ the books of ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ such as the Torah and the Gospel.

celaleyn:197-197.t: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُمْ﴾ for the disbelievers of Mecca ﴿آيَةً﴾ of that ﴿أَنْ يَعْلَمَهُ عُلَمَاءُ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ such as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and his companions who believed, for they inform of that. And يَكُنْ is with the lower-dotted letter [yāʾ] and the accusative of آيَةً, and with the upper-dotted letter [tāʾ] and the nominative آيَةٌ.

celaleyn:198-198.t: ﴿وَلَوْ نَزَّلْنَاهُ عَلَى بَعْضِ الْأَعْجَمِينَ﴾ plural of أَعْجَم

celaleyn:199-199.t: ﴿فَقَرَأَهُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca ﴿مَا كَانُوا بِهِ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ out of disdain for following him.

celaleyn:200-200.t: ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. like Our putting the denial of it [into their hearts] through the recitation of the non-Arab ﴿سَلَكْنَاهُ﴾ We have put the denial of it ﴿فِي قُلُوبِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca, through the recitation of the Prophet.

celaleyn:201-201.t: ﴿لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ حَتَّى يَرَوُا الْعَذَابَ الْأَلِيمَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:202-202.t: ﴿فَيَأْتِيَهُمْ بَغْتَةً وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:203-203.t: ﴿فَيَقُولُوا هَلْ نَحْنُ مُنْظَرُونَ﴾ so that we may believe? And it is said to them: No. They said: When is this punishment? Allah the Exalted said:

celaleyn:204-204.t: ﴿أَفَبِعَذَابِنَا يَسْتَعْجِلُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:206-206.t: ﴿ثُمَّ جَاءَهُمْ مَا كَانُوا يُوعَدُونَ﴾ of punishment

celaleyn:207-207.t: ﴿مَا﴾ interrogative (istifhāmiyya), in the sense of «what thing» ﴿أَغْنَى عَنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوا يُمَتَّعُونَ﴾ in warding off the punishment or lightening it? i.e. it did not avail.

celaleyn:208-208.t: ﴿وَمَا أَهْلَكْنَا مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ إِلَّا لَهَا مُنْذِرُونَ﴾ messengers warning its people

celaleyn:209-209.t: ﴿ذِكْرَى﴾ an admonition for them ﴿وَمَا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ﴾ in destroying them after warning them. And [the following] was revealed in refutation of the polytheists' saying:

celaleyn:211-211.t: ﴿وَمَا يَنْبَغِي﴾ it is not fitting ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ to bring it down ﴿وَمَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ﴾ that.

celaleyn:212-212.t: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ عَنِ السَّمْعِ﴾ of the speech of the angels ﴿لَمَعْزُولُونَ﴾ by the shooting stars.

celaleyn:213-213.t: ﴿فَلَا تَدْعُ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَهًا آخَرَ فَتَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُعَذَّبِينَ﴾ if you did that to which they have called you.

celaleyn:214-214.t: ﴿وَأَنْذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ الْأَقْرَبِينَ﴾ and they are the Banū Hāshim and the Banū al-Muṭṭalib; and he warned them openly — narrated by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

celaleyn:215-215.t: ﴿وَاخْفِضْ جَنَاحَكَ﴾ be gentle ﴿لِمَنِ اتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ who affirm Allah's oneness.

celaleyn:216-216.t: ﴿فَإِنْ عَصَوْكَ﴾ i.e. your kinsfolk ﴿فَقُلْ﴾ to them ﴿إِنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ of worshipping other than Allah.

celaleyn:217-217.t: ﴿وَتَوَكَّلْ﴾ with wāw and with fāʾ ﴿عَلَى الْعَزِيزِ الرَّحِيمِ﴾ Allah, i.e. entrust all your affairs to Him

celaleyn:219-219.t: ﴿وَتَقَلُّبَكَ﴾ in the pillars of the prayer, standing, sitting, bowing and prostrating ﴿فِي السَّاجِدِينَ﴾ i.e. among those praying.

celaleyn:220-220.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:221-221.t: ﴿هَلْ أُنَبِّئُكُمْ﴾ i.e. O disbelievers of Mecca ﴿عَلَى مَنْ تَنَزَّلُ الشَّيَاطِينُ﴾ with omission of one of the two tāʾs of the original.

celaleyn:222-222.t: ﴿تَنَزَّلُ عَلَى كُلِّ أَفَّاكٍ﴾ great liar ﴿أَثِيمٍ﴾ wicked, such as Musaylima and other soothsayers.

celaleyn:223-223.t: ﴿يُلْقُونَ﴾ i.e. the devils ﴿السَّمْعَ﴾ i.e. what they have heard from the angels, to the soothsayers ﴿وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ كَاذِبُونَ﴾ they add many lies to what is heard; and this was before the devils were barred from the heaven.

celaleyn:224-224.t: ﴿وَالشُّعَرَاءُ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ الْغَاوُونَ﴾ in their poetry, so they recite it and transmit it from them; so they are blameworthy.

celaleyn:225-225.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ﴾ know ﴿أَنَّهُمْ فِي كُلِّ وَادٍ﴾ of the valleys of speech and its arts ﴿يَهِيمُونَ﴾ roam, overstepping the limit in praise and satire

celaleyn:226-226.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ﴾ «we did» ﴿مَا لَا يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ i.e. they lie.

celaleyn:227-227.t: ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ﴾ among the poets ﴿وَذَكَرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا﴾ poetry did not distract them from remembrance ﴿وَانْتَصَرُوا﴾ by satirising the disbelievers ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا ظُلِمُوا﴾ by the disbelievers' satire of them along with the [rest of the] believers; so they are not blameworthy. Allah the Exalted said: {لَا يُحِبُّ اللَّهُ الْجَهْرَ بِالسُّوءِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ إِلَّا مَنْ ظُلِمَ}, and the Exalted said: {فَمَنِ اعْتَدَى عَلَيْكُمْ فَاعْتَدُوا عَلَيْهِ بِمِثْلِ مَا اعْتَدَى عَلَيْكُمْ} ﴿وَسَيَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا﴾ of the poets and others ﴿أَيَّ مُنْقَلَبٍ﴾ place of return ﴿يَنْقَلِبُونَ﴾ they will be returned to after death.
